title: Palliative Management of End-of-Life Dyspnoea and Pain

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults at the end of life with breathlessness and/or pain: reversible causes, non-drug measures, oxygen only for hypoxaemia, and opioid/benzodiazepine therapy. Verified against Saudi MOH Protocol-010 (opioid doses) and NICE NG31. pathophysiology.summary: End-of-life breathlessness and pain are distressing symptoms with mixed causes — disease progression, complications (effusion, pulmonary oedema, infection, fracture) and anxiety. Opioids reduce both the perception of breathlessness and pain.
keyMechanisms: Breathlessness arises from increased respiratory drive, mechanical load (effusion, ascites), hypoxaemia and anxiety.
Opioids reduce respiratory drive and the sensation of breathlessness; benzodiazepines relieve associated anxiety (NICE NG31).
Oxygen helps only when hypoxaemia is present (NICE NG31 1.5.16).
Pain may come from tumour, bone, nerves or reversible causes such as urinary retention (NICE NG31 1.5.11).

symptoms: Breathlessness at rest, panic, fear of suffocation.
Pain reported by the person or shown by behaviour (grimacing, guarding, restlessness).
physicalSigns: Tachypnoea, accessory muscle use; signs of effusion, pulmonary oedema or infection.
SpO2 if it would change care; pain behaviours using a validated tool when communication is limited.
redFlags: Sudden severe breathlessness — consider reversible cause if consistent with goals (pulmonary oedema, effusion)
Uncontrolled symptoms despite titration — specialist palliative care
precipitants: Disease progression (lung cancer, COPD, heart failure)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Dull percussion; drainage may relieve if appropriate.
Episodic with fear; responds to calm presence and benzodiazepine.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Offer oxygen only for known or suspected symptomatic hypoxaemia (NICE NG31 1.5.16).
ruleIn.normalValue: SpO2 94% or more (88–92% if chronic hypercapnia)

clinicalManagement.title: Reversible causes and non-drug care
actions: Treat reversible causes of breathlessness (pulmonary oedema, effusion) and pain (urinary retention) when consistent with goals (NICE NG31).
Fan, positioning, calm presence; do not routinely start oxygen (NICE NG31 1.5.16).

clinicalManagement.title: Drug treatment
actions: Breathlessness: opioid, benzodiazepine or both (NICE NG31 1.5.17).
Opioid-naïve: morphine 5–10 mg PO every 4 h as needed, or IV 2.5–5 mg every 3–4 h (MOH Protocol-010 p. 9); start low and titrate (NICE NG31 1.5.7).
Anxiety component: benzodiazepine trial (e.g. lorazepam label dose 1–2 mg/day in divided doses if elderly or debilitated).
Pain: follow cancer-pain principles — match drug to severity, regular plus PRN, laxative (see Cancer Pain topic).
More than 2–3 PRN doses in 24 h: syringe pump (NICE NG31 1.5.6).

regimens.dose: 5–10 mg PO (usual 5–15 mg) or 2.5–5 mg IV
regimens.frequency: Every 4 h as needed (IV every 3–4 h)
adjustments: MOH dose is stated for pain; NICE NG31 recommends opioid for breathlessness without a dose
monitoring: Symptom score, sedation, respiratory rate, bowels
contraindications: Acute or severe asthma without monitoring/resuscitation
Known or suspected GI obstruction including paralytic ileus

learningObjectives: Relieve end-of-life breathlessness and pain with reversible-cause review, non-drug measures and titrated opioids.
pitfalls: Under-treating breathlessness for fear of respiratory depression.
Missing urinary retention as a cause of pain.
keyPoints: Syringe pump if more than 2–3 PRN doses/day.
